title: Dark Fantasy ARPG Mistfall Hunter Launches on PS5, Xbox and PC With Diablo Creator's Backing
excerpt: Bellring Games' extraction RPG, published by Diablo creator David Brevik's Skystone Games, drops players into a cursed world where death means losing everything — and nearly 430,000 beta testers couldn't get enough.
body:
• Mistfall Hunter launched July 29 on PS5, Xbox Series X|S, and PC via Steam, priced at $24.99 for the Standard Edition and $39.99 for the Deluxe Edition.
  • The third-person PvPvE extraction ARPG is published by Skystone Games, co-founded by Diablo creator David Brevik, and developed by emerging studio Bellring Games.
  • Nearly 430,000 players tested the open beta during Steam Next Fest in June, pushing the game onto Steam's Top Demos and Top Trending charts.
  • The game features six playable classes, three-player co-op with full cross-play, and a firm no pay-to-win policy with progression driven entirely by skill.

Mistfall Hunter, a dark fantasy extraction ARPG from developer Bellring Games and publisher Skystone Games, launched on July 29 across PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, and PC via Steam. The game merges Soulslike melee combat with the high-stakes tension of extraction shooters, tasking players with looting a cursed realm and escaping alive — or losing everything to death.

The Standard Edition is priced at $24.99, while the Deluxe Edition costs $39.99 and includes exclusive cosmetics, 2,500 Fate Coins, and additional in-game bonuses. A 10 percent launch discount is available across all platforms through August 12.

A Shattered World Built on Divine Blood

Set in Weavereach, a world consumed by a corrosive fog called the Gyldenmist, the game's premise is built on mythic collapse. The gods waged war against the outer gods, and every deity fell. Their blood mutated the land, spawning corrupted creatures that stalk the mist.

https://x.com/XBOXWire/status/2082859009896554536

Players take on the role of Gyldhunters — heroes resurrected by a mysterious girl named Dew — tasked with harvesting Gyldenblood from these twisted creatures to mend the Web of Fate. Each run is a gamble: venture into the fog solo or in three-player squads, fight monstrous enemies and rival players, gather loot, and locate a Returner Woodling to extract safely. Die before reaching it, and every item collected is gone.

"Squad up in three-player teams or push in solo, choose your class, and extract before something out there extracts you."

— Bellring Games

Six Classes and Fluid Combat

Mistfall Hunter offers six distinct classes: Mercenary, Sorcerer, Blackarrow, Shadowstrix, Seer, and the newest addition, the Withered Knight. The last of these, exiled Rose Knights from the Kingdom of Gaenaria, wields a two-handed greatsword and operates through a sigil-and-detonation combat loop that rewards patient, strategic play.

Combat is third-person and precision-driven, with a free-aim system that lets players target enemy weak points. Weapons can be swapped mid-combat, and a diverse arsenal of tactical items adds layers of strategic depth to each encounter. The system draws clear inspiration from Soulslike design — parries are timing-dependent, dodges must be precise, and every engagement carries real consequence.

Brevik's Skystone Games Bets on Extraction

The game's publishing pedigree adds weight to its ambitions. Skystone Games was co-founded by David Brevik, the creator of Diablo, and veteran industry figure Bill Wang. Their involvement signals confidence in the extraction ARPG as an emerging genre — one that fuses the loot-driven compulsion of action RPGs with the adrenaline of survival-style gameplay where player-versus-player encounters add unpredictability to every run.

The bet appears to be paying early dividends. During the open beta from June 14 to 22, nearly 430,000 players participated through Steam Next Fest alone, earning the game spots on Steam's Top Demos and Top Trending Upcoming charts. Streaming platforms like Twitch and YouTube also saw significant attention for the title, with early consensus pointing to polished, responsive combat.

No Pay-to-Win and Cross-Play

Bellring Games has committed to a no pay-to-win model, with all progression tied to skill and in-game effort rather than spending. The Deluxe Edition's extras are cosmetic, and the Standard Edition provides the complete gameplay experience. Full cross-play across all three platforms means the player pool remains unified from launch — a critical feature for a game that depends on populated lobbies for its PvPvE encounters.

Seasonal content updates are planned post-launch, with the developer's earlier roadmap outlining new maps, monsters, bosses, custom cosmetics, and additional game modes rolling out through 2026.

A Growing Genre for Indian Gamers

For the Indian diaspora's growing gaming community, Mistfall Hunter represents an accessible entry point into the extraction genre at a competitive price. At $24.99, it undercuts many AAA releases, while its cross-play support means players in India, North America, and Europe can squad up regardless of platform. The game's Soulslike combat and dark fantasy aesthetics align with the genre preferences that have driven strong interest in titles like Elden Ring and Diablo IV among Indian gamers worldwide.

What's Next

With the launch discount running through August 12, Bellring Games is banking on early momentum to build a sustained player base. The studio's roadmap extends through late 2026, with new difficulty modes, a Solemn Needles map expansion, and reworked class archetypes on the horizon. Whether Mistfall Hunter can carve a lasting niche in the competitive extraction landscape will depend on how quickly it delivers on those post-launch promises — but the open beta numbers suggest the foundation is solid.
nri_angle: The game's competitive pricing and cross-play support make it accessible for Indian gamers worldwide, aligning with the growing Soulslike and ARPG interest in the diaspora gaming community.
